selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main lesson are students told to notice from the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Human abilities were not given just to chase worldly comfort like animals do.

questions.question: What job was simple and limited in the comparison?
questions.answer: Buying a suit with a small amount of money.

questions.question: What extra responsibility came with the paper placed in the second servant’s pocket?
questions.answer: He was expected to learn and carry out a specific assignment.

questions.question: How is the story connected to human life?
questions.answer: Human life also contains valuable gifts that must be used for their true purpose.

questions.question: In the lesson drawn from the comparison, what does the “capital” of life refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the abilities, gifts, and potential placed in a person’s life.

questions.question: Which lifestyle is condemned in the final warning?
questions.answer: A life centered on physical pleasure and short-term worldly enjoyment.

questions.question: If a human uses those gifts wrongly, what makes the fall especially severe?
questions.answer: The fall is severe because the person turns great blessings into a cause of disgrace.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to examine carefully?
questions.answer: A comparison meant to explain the real purpose of human faculties.

questions.question: What false idea about life is the comparison correcting?
questions.answer: The idea that human gifts are only for worldly gain and physical comfort.

questions.question: Why was the written paper important to the second servant’s duty?
questions.answer: It contained directions he needed in order to use the money properly.

questions.question: What was his second serious mistake?
questions.answer: He copied another servant instead of understanding his own duty.

questions.question: In the warning that follows, who is directly addressed?
questions.answer: The speaker addresses the self and a close companion.

questions.question: What are these gifts not supposed to be spent on?
questions.answer: They are not supposed to be consumed only by bodily urges and passing worldly pleasures.

questions.question: What happens when a person with higher gifts chooses lower aims?
questions.answer: That person drops beneath the level he was meant to live at.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the story about the two servants?
questions.answer: It teaches that people should understand the true purpose of the gifts given to them.

questions.question: How much money did the first servant receive, and what did he do with it?
questions.answer: He got twenty gold coins and bought a very good suit.

questions.question: What did the second servant spend all the money on?
questions.answer: He used it all to buy a suit of clothes.

questions.question: What false use of these gifts is rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Using them only for temporary worldly enjoyment and bodily appetite.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does a person become worse than animals?
questions.answer: By using greater human gifts only for low desires instead of higher purposes.

questions.question: Why is falling below animals described as possible for a human?
questions.answer: Because a human can betray greater gifts by choosing lower goals.

questions.question: What claim about human life is made in the opening sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: Human powers were not given merely to gain worldly living in an animal-like way.

questions.question: Who gave the money in the comparison?
questions.answer: An employer gave it to his servants.

questions.question: What result came from spending all the money on clothes?
questions.answer: He got an inferior suit and failed in the task he had been sent to do.

questions.question: What are readers warned not to imitate?
questions.answer: They are warned not to live for bodily desire the way animals do.

title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self
